item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
[Image: Rectangle divided into 12 squares with some squares shaded]

Which circle has approximately the same fraction of its area shaded as the rectangle above?
item.figure_description:
At the top, a rectangle is divided into a grid of 3 rows and 4 columns, forming 12 equal-sized squares. The bottom row has all 4 squares shaded gray. The middle row has the leftmost square shaded gray and the other 3 squares unshaded (white). The top row has all 4 squares unshaded. In total, 5 of the 12 squares are shaded.

Each option shows a circle with a center point and radial lines dividing it into sectors, with one sector shaded gray:
- Option A: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and another radius pointing down and slightly left (about 6:30). The larger sector on the right side is shaded gray (covering slightly more than half of the circle).
- Option B: The circle is divided by a vertical diameter passing through the center from 12 o'clock to 6 o'clock. The right half of the circle is shaded gray (exactly 1/2 of the circle).
- Option C: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and a horizontal radius pointing left (9 o'clock). The sector extending clockwise from 12 o'clock to 9 o'clock is shaded gray (3/4 of the circle).
- Option D: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and another radius pointing down and to the right (about 4:30 to 5 o'clock). The sector between them on the right side is shaded gray (covering somewhat less than half of the circle, approximately 5/12 of the area).
- Option E: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and another radius pointing up and slightly left (about 11 o'clock). The major sector extending clockwise from 12 o'clock to 11 o'clock is shaded gray (covering almost the entire circle, about 11/12 of the area).
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Which shows 2/3 of the square shaded?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Square divided horizontally into six equal strips with the top two strips shaded]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Square with an unshaded triangle at the bottom and shaded regions above]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Square divided vertically into three strips with the two narrow outer strips shaded]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Square with an unshaded triangle spanning from the bottom edge to the top center and two shaded triangles on the sides]

options.label: E
options.text: [Image: Square divided vertically into three equal strips with the two outer strips shaded]

reference_items.figure_description:
Five squares, labeled A through E, are shown in a row:
- Square A is divided horizontally into 6 equal strips. The top 2 strips are shaded gray, and the bottom 4 strips are unshaded white.
- Square B has line segments extending from the bottom-left corner to the center, from the bottom-right corner to the center, and from the center to the top-right corner. The triangle formed at the bottom is white, and the remaining area of the square is shaded gray.
- Square C is divided vertically into three regions by two vertical lines: two narrow gray strips on the left and right edges, each approximately one-sixth the width of the square, and a wider unshaded white region in the middle.
- Square D contains an unshaded white isosceles triangle whose base is the bottom edge of the square and whose apex touches the midpoint of the top edge. The two right-triangular regions to the left and right of this triangle are shaded gray.
- Square E is divided vertically into 3 strips of equal width. The leftmost and rightmost strips are shaded gray, and the middle strip is unshaded white.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
What fraction of the circle is shaded?

[Image: A circle divided into two sectors, one shaded and one unshaded]
reference_items.figure_description: A circle with a center dot. Two radii divide the circle into two sectors. One radius extends straight up from the center to the 12 o'clock position. The other radius extends to the left, slightly below the horizontal 9 o'clock position. The larger sector, which runs clockwise from the top radius around through the right side and bottom to the lower-left radius, is shaded solid gray. The smaller remaining sector in the upper-left area is white (unshaded).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Large right triangle divided into smaller triangles]

In the figure above, each of the smaller triangles has the same area. What is the ratio of the shaded area to the unshaded area?
reference_items.figure_description:
A large right triangle with its vertical leg on the left and horizontal leg at the bottom, divided into smaller congruent right triangles arranged in 4 horizontal rows and 4 vertical columns:
- Row 4 (top): Column 1 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its right angle at the bottom-left and its hypotenuse along the hypotenuse of the large triangle.
- Row 3: Column 1 contains a rectangle divided by a diagonal into a shaded triangle (bottom-left) and an unshaded triangle (top-right); Column 2 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its hypotenuse along the large triangle's hypotenuse.
- Row 2: Columns 1 and 2 each contain a rectangle divided by a diagonal into a shaded triangle (bottom-left) and an unshaded triangle (top-right); Column 3 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its hypotenuse along the large triangle's hypotenuse.
- Row 1 (bottom): Columns 1, 2, and 3 each contain a rectangle divided by a diagonal into a shaded triangle (bottom-left) and an unshaded triangle (top-right); Column 4 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its hypotenuse along the large triangle's hypotenuse.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Which angle in the figure has a measure closest to 45°?

[Image: Circle divided into angles p, q, r, and s]
reference_items.figure_description: A circle contains a vertical diameter dividing it into left and right halves. From the center, two additional line segments (radii) are drawn: one extending to the left edge at roughly 9 o'clock (slightly below horizontal), and another extending down and to the right at approximately a 45-degree angle from the vertical. Four central angles are labeled: angle q is in the upper-left quadrant (between the upward vertical radius and the left radius, roughly 90°); angle p is in the lower-left quadrant (between the left radius and the downward vertical radius, roughly 90°); angle r is in the upper-right (between the upward vertical radius and the lower-right radius, an obtuse angle of roughly 135°); and angle s is in the lower-right (between the downward vertical radius and the lower-right radius, roughly 45°).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Which picture shows that 2/5 is equivalent to 4/10 ?

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: 2-by-5 grid with 5 squares shaded in a checkerboard pattern]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Rectangle with 2 solid circles and 3 open circles]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four labeled options (A, B, C, D):
- Option A shows a rectangle divided into a 2-by-5 grid of 10 equal squares. The two squares in the first column and the two squares in the fifth column are completely shaded black (4 of 10 squares shaded).
- Option B shows a rectangle divided into a 2-by-5 grid of 10 equal squares. The top-left square (row 1, column 1) and bottom-right square (row 2, column 5) are shaded black (2 of 10 squares shaded).
- Option C shows a rectangle divided into a 2-by-5 grid of 10 equal squares. In the top row, the 1st, 3rd, and 5th squares are shaded black; in the bottom row, the 2nd and 4th squares are shaded black (5 of 10 squares shaded in a checkerboard pattern).
- Option D shows a rectangular box containing five small circles scattered inside: two circles are solid black and three circles are open white circles with a black outline.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Rectangle ABCD containing two tangent circles P and Q]

In the figure above, ABCD is a rectangle, and circles P and Q each have a radius of 5 cm. What is the area of the rectangle?
reference_items.figure_description: A rectangle ABCD is oriented horizontally with vertices labeled A at the top-left, B at the top-right, C at the bottom-right, and D at the bottom-left. Inside the rectangle are two identical circles labeled P and Q, with their centers marked by dots labeled P and Q. The two circles are tangent to each other horizontally at the midline of the rectangle. Circle P touches the left side AD, the top side AB, and the bottom side CD. Circle Q touches circle P, the right side BC, the top side AB, and the bottom side CD. A vertical line segment is drawn from center P up to the point of tangency on top side AB, labeled "5 cm".
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A shaded rectangle that is 6 cm by 16 cm. Part of the rectangle is unshaded. The unshaded part of the rectangle forms a right triangle on the left that is 6 centimeters by 8 centimeters.]

In the figure above, what is the area of the shaded region in cm^2?
reference_items.figure_description: A rectangle with a height of 6 cm and a total length of 16 cm along the top, both labeled with dimension arrows. An unshaded right triangle occupies the bottom-left portion of the rectangle; its vertical leg is the left side of the rectangle (6 cm) and its horizontal leg along the bottom has a length of 8 cm labeled with a dimension arrow. The remainder of the rectangle is shaded solid black.

The figure shows a shaded rectangle inside a parallelogram.

What is the area of the shaded rectangle?

Answer: ____

reference_items.scoring_notes: Note: There is no distinction made between responses with or without units.
reference_items.figure_description: A parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides and slanted left and right sides. Inside the parallelogram is a shaded rectangle sharing parts of the top and bottom edges of the parallelogram. A dimension line at the bottom shows that the distance from the bottom-left vertex of the parallelogram to the bottom-right corner of the shaded rectangle is 8 cm. A dimension line along the top shows that the segment of the parallelogram's top edge extending to the right of the shaded rectangle has a length of 3 cm. A vertical dimension line on the right indicates that the height of the parallelogram (and of the rectangle) is 4 cm.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
